clue.text: Standard document variously biased towards graduate

parts.note: PRO and FOR are two different words that each mean biased towards, in favour of; 'variously' asks for both
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A standard form that somehow tilts in favour of applicants holding a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variously' tells you to give 'biased towards' two ways: PRO and FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a standard template document, filled in the same way each time.

clue.text: At end of dinner for one, throw out another sprout

indicators.note: at end of picks the last letter of dinner

parts.note: last letter of dinner
EG, for example, means for one

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once a dinner for one is over, a sprout gets thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrowth is new growth after cutting, another shoot coming up.

clue.text: Licence not paid for by government, we're told

parts.note: free means not paid for

indicators.note: we're told means heard, said aloud, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule, government

explanation.surface: A licence that the government says it is not charging for.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is often wrongly written 'free reign'; the clue plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein is complete freedom to act, the liberty that licence also means.

clue.text: Hastily shift marsh plant

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a reed-like plant of wet ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hurrying along and the grassy plant growing in swamps.

clue.text: As nice as Ritz's top cocktail

definitions.note: As is the chemical symbol for the element

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up
top picks the first letter of Ritz's

parts.note: first letter of Ritz's

explanation.surface: A drink at the Ritz hotel praised as being as nice as its best cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word: As is the chemical symbol, not a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the symbol on the periodic table for the poisonous element arsenic.

clue.text: Regularly reuse, in gym, a training shoe

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of reuse

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of reuse

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the pair goes inside the other word

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
drill is training, as in army drill

explanation.surface: Keep reusing, in the gym, a single trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: Student, once being briefly with nothing to eat, being forgotten

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so one piece swallows the other
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: living means being, existing
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A former student, short of money, has nothing to eat and is forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' takes LIVING down to LIVIN, and 'to eat' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being forgotten by everyone.

clue.text: Overburdened boat crew outwardly united

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so this word wraps the other

parts.note: wed means united in marriage
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing crew, overloaded, still looks together on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighted means loaded down, carrying excessive weight.

clue.text: Be like a son avoiding mass again

indicators.note: avoiding means the named letters stay out of the word, so they are removed

parts.note: to mass again is to reassemble, gather together once more

explanation.surface: A boy who looks like his father keeps away from church services again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like a church service, but it is the verb, to gather; REASSEMBLE loses its A and one S.
explanation.definitionFit: To resemble someone is to look or be similar to them.

clue.text: Queen bearing grand letters exits

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the queen holds the next letter inside

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
ESSES are letters, plural of the letter S spelt out

explanation.surface: A queen carrying important letters leaves the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Egresses as a noun are ways out, the formal word for exit points.

clue.text: Start of Lennon's Imagine reworked, conveying modern message

indicators.note: reworked means the letters are made over in a new order
start of picks the first letter of Lennon's

parts.note: first letter of Lennon's

explanation.surface: A new arrangement of John Lennon's song Imagine, starting from its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Emailing is sending electronic mail, a modern way to send a message.

clue.text: Fragrant wild flower with berries wet, bedraggled

indicators.note: bedraggled means messed up and dishevelled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling wild plant whose berries have been soaked by rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbrier is the eglantine, a wild rose with scented leaves and flowers.

clue.text: Old nationalist boycotts strike, run internally

parts.note: to black is to boycott, in trade-union sense

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: hit means strike
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A veteran nationalist refuses to support a strike that is run from inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackshirts were Mussolini's Italian fascist militia, members of an extreme nationalist movement.

clue.text: Clothing covering Dougal's rear?

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the outer word goes round the letter

parts.note: kit is clothing, as in sports kit

indicators.note: rear picks the last letter of Dougal's name

parts.note: last letter of Dougal, the name without its possessive

explanation.surface: What a Scotsman named Dougal wears over his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: KIT goes round L, the end of Dougal, and Dougal is a typically Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is the Highland garment, a knee-length tartan skirt worn by Scottish men.

clue.text: Country hosts with good conversation

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as a guest, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: A nation entertains guests and they have a pleasant talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is informal British slang for a chat or gossip.

clue.text: Ready to support service for card users

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Being ready to help out a service for people using cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective; in British slang the ready is cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashback is a shop's service of giving money to a customer paying by debit card.

clue.text: Current motorway schedule easily followed?

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a table is a schedule, as in timetable

explanation.surface: A timetable for current motorway works that is easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 reads as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitable means capable of being copied, so it can be followed with ease.

clue.text: Picked up in the field, finally being rested

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of being

parts.note: last letter of being
leaned means rested against something

explanation.surface: A farmhand at last takes a rest after harvesting.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain from a harvested field, so gleaned means collected there.

clue.text: Adult follows mounted troops moving part of generator

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so this word goes second
mounted means going up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are troops
mature means adult, grown up

explanation.surface: A grown-up comes after cavalry on horseback moving a generator part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted troops' looks like cavalry, but 'mounted' turns RA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The armature is the rotating coil assembly in a dynamo or electric motor.

clue.text: Scriptures record one saint taking off shortly

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: less means taking off, minus

explanation.surface: A record of a saint quickly leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistles are the letters of the New Testament, part of holy writ.

clue.text: Place in office on public view lately?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to install in a post
second meaning: ..., as a dead person, the late, lies ... for the public to view

explanation.walkthrough: 'lately' puns on the late, the dead: a body lying in state is on public view.
explanation.definitionFit: To instate is to install someone formally; split as two words it means lying in state.

clue.text: Aforementioned copper since retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a copper is a police officer; DI is a Detective Inspector
as means since, because

explanation.surface: The policeman mentioned before has since stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an adjective means the one already mentioned, as in the said gentleman.

clue.text: Travelling like men and woman from Battersea, maybe

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman from a London district who goes about the way men do.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea is the London home of a famous dogs' shelter, Battersea Dogs and Cats Home, so the woman is one who looks after its dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel maid is a woman employed to care for dogs, as at the Battersea shelter.

clue.text: Staff officer, pushy, busy with collaring squadron leader

indicators.note: collaring means grabbing round the neck, so the pair surrounds the letter

parts.note: brash means pushy, self-assertive

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of squadron

parts.note: first letter of squadron
AT means busy, as in at it or at work

explanation.surface: A pushy officer is busy arresting the head of an air squadron.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is old military slang for a senior officer, from the gold braid on the cap.

clue.text: Stage dance sequence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stage or phase in a process
second meaning: a sequence of movements in a dance

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a phase of progress and a pattern of foot movements in dancing.

clue.text: Drunk during social, heading off with guile

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the word goes inside
heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a social is a party
full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk at a party slips away cunningly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as the person at the party, but it is the British slang word for intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Artfully means cunningly or craftily, done with cleverness that deceives.

clue.text: The Spanish invested in wine for drinks cabinet..

indicators.note: invested in means placed within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: claret is a red Bordeaux wine
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish buyers put money into wine stored in a drinks cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard compartment for keeping bottles of wine.

clue.text: English therefore brought round squash drink machine

indicators.note: brought round means placed around, so the letters wrap the other word

parts.note: so means therefore
to press is to squash

explanation.surface: An Englishman brings round a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the fruit drink (a British cordial) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a coffee maker that forces steam through ground beans, as well as the coffee.
